newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast lt. crudes off, second ANS deal seen.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast lt. crudes off, second ANS deal seen.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crude prices eased in line with lower WTI/Cushing values Thursday, with the week's second Alaskan crude deal rumored done by BP, traders said.
Traders said BP reportedly sold a full cargo of Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude at minus 0.90 cents, a 10-cent increase over yesterday's spot sale to a major West Coast refinery.
Traders said the refinery bought early because it might need the supply at its Hawaii refinery, which needs supply commited early because of delivery complications.
But ANS outright prices fell to $19.70/19.90 a barrel, down 30 cents from Wednesday as WTI markets followed a weak sour crude and heating oil market.
Line 63 prices stood unchanged at postings plus $0.95 - $1.05. One trader said the posting plus market, with gravity adjustments, stood at a slight premium to ANS.
He said Chevron might lower its California Buena Vista postings as a result.
Kern River heavy crude stayed steady after falling Monday, with prices talked 13.84/14.04 a barrel, traders said.
A rumor circulated that a refinery sold March barrels at minus 45 cents, a sharp increase over a 90-cent deal heard done recently.
